source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn stalk borer (ដង្គូវស៊ីងដើម, Diatraea lineolata; also covered under the general name Corn borer / Corn stalk borer, Order: Lepidoptera): the larva bores into the stalk and feeds inside it, hollowing out the pith. Larval color is pale/whitish, and larvae are about 25-30 mm long. Adult moths mate and lay eggs, and eggs hatch in about 8-9 days, up to 15 days.

The larva bores into the corn stem and feeds inside for its full larval life, then pupates inside the stalk itself, and pupation lasts about 8-10 days before the adult moth emerges. Damage from this pest can vary in severity by field condition -- infestation can affect up to about 50% of the stalks in a field in severe cases. Feeding damage weakens the stem near the plant's growing point and, when a field has already been weakened by nutrient deficiency, damage tends to be worse. If damage occurs before ear formation, it can prevent the plant from developing an ear at all; if it occurs after ear formation, it can cause the stalk to break/lodge below the ear.

Prevention and control measures:
- Remove weeds present in the field, especially near where clean seed lots are kept, and destroy related host-plant residue.
- Collect larvae and pupae and destroy them by burning.
- Use resistant/tolerant varieties.
- Practice appropriate crop timing.
- Manage the field to reduce plant stress and weakening, since weakened plants suffer more severe damage from this pest.
